overview: Oil pulled back in early Monday trading after President Trump signed an executive order waiving sanctions and tariffs on Russia, a move markets expect to ease supply tightness. Brent fell about 1.2% to $108.35 and WTI slipped 0.6% to $101.18, paring last week's rally that had pushed both benchmarks to their highest since May. The waiver undercuts a key bullish pillar — restricted Russian exports — but Hormuz disruptions continue to provide a floor: Kpler data showed crude flows through the strait dropping to 12.6 million barrels a day on October 13, down from 15 million at end-September. Coal held at $150 near a three-year high.

Precious metals firmed after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's comments led traders to cut the implied probability of an October rate hike to under 20%. Gold rose 0.2% to about $4,174, silver gained 0.6% to $57.33, and palladium bounced from a year-low. Corn fell for a fourth straight session to 473¢ as harvest pressure intensified, while wheat and soybeans held near Friday's levels. Bitcoin steadied at $82,178, shrugging off Friday's equity selloff and the 39th anniversary of the 1987 Black Monday crash.

watchItems.title: Russia sanctions waiver
watchItems.text: Trump's executive order may add Russian barrels to a market already absorbing Hormuz disruptions. Watch for changes in tanker bookings and Black Sea export data this week.

watchItems.title: FOMC, Oct 27–28
watchItems.text: Warsh's remarks have reduced October hike odds below 20%. The statement language and any signal on December will drive gold, silver and rate-sensitive metals.

watchItems.title: Hormuz attacks at record pace
watchItems.text: Twelve vessels attacked in one week. Kpler shows flows at 12.6M b/d, down from 15M at end-September. Further escalation would test whether the Russia waiver can offset lost barrels.

watchItems.title: US harvest progress
watchItems.text: Next USDA crop progress report will show whether corn (33% done) is catching up to the five-year average (39%). Soybean harvest at 46% is pointing to a record crop. Key for the Corn and Soybean pages.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold edged up 0.2% to about $4,174 in early Monday trading after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks curbed rate-hike expectations, with traders cutting the implied probability of an October hike to under 20%. A weaker dollar and Warsh's support for holding rates steadied the metal, which closed the prior week lower after hot CPI data. Gold remains about 26% below its January record near $5,608.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver gained 0.6% to $57.33 on Monday, lifted by dovish Fed signals and a weaker dollar. The metal is still down about 12% on the month and more than half below its late-January record near $121.6. The Silver Institute projects a sixth straight supply deficit this year, providing a floor, but rate-hike uncertainty keeps rallies in check.

desk.name: Oil
desk.sum: Brent fell about 1.2% to $108.35 and WTI slipped to about $101 after President Trump signed an executive order waiving sanctions and tariffs on Russia, a move expected to boost Russian fuel exports. The drop pared Friday's rally that had pushed benchmarks to their highest since May. Hormuz disruptions continue — 12 vessels attacked in one week — but the prospect of additional Russian supply has shifted sentiment.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper eased to $6.52 in early Monday trading, essentially flat. Chilean supply remains tight with ongoing strikes at BHP's Escondida and Antofagasta's Centinela, and demand from data centres and grid storage keeps the metal close to its September record of $6.85. A stronger dollar ahead of the FOMC meeting is the main near-term headwind.

desk.name: Coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal held at $150.40 a tonne, unchanged from Friday and near a three-year high. LNG remains expensive due to Middle East disruption, keeping coal about 80% cheaper and driving pre-winter stocking by Asian and European utilities. Indonesia's tightened export rules cut August shipments 23%, constraining supply further.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum gained 0.6% to $1,643 in early Monday trading, supported by dovish Fed signals and a weaker dollar. The metal is still down about 8.5% on the month, and the WPIC expects total platinum demand to fall 18% this year. A 2% decline in global EV sales in September could support autocatalyst demand, providing some offset.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium bounced 0.6% to $1,125, recovering modestly from a year-low. Fed Chair Warsh's comments curbing rate-hike bets gave the metal some relief, but it is still down about 14% on the month and 25% on the year. EV adoption continues to erode catalytic-converter demand, and steady investment outflows show no sign of reversing.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.sum: Attacks in the Strait hit a record pace in October. UKMTO logged 12 vessels attacked between October 5 and 11, including six on October 11 alone. Kpler measured about 12.6 million barrels a day on October 13, down from 15 million at end-September and about 74% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline. The GFS Pride was sunk and the GFS Giselle suffered hull damage. CENTCOM reported 135 vessels redirected during blockade enforcement.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn slipped to 473¢ in overnight trading, falling for a fourth straight session. The USDA's yield estimate of 181.2 bushels per acre points to a large crop, and projected ending stocks of 1.85 billion bushels continue to outweigh incremental export gains. Fund liquidation and harvest pressure are intensifying the selloff.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: CBOT wheat held near 660¢ in the overnight session, unchanged from Friday and about 31% higher on the year. Weekly export sales fell 29% to 11.8 million bushels, at the bottom of analyst estimates. Winter wheat planting is progressing and harvest pressure across grains is setting the seasonal tone.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: Soybeans held near 1,261¢, little changed from Friday. A fast harvest — 46% complete — is pointing to a record US crop. China booked 8–10 cargoes for December and the USDA confirmed new sales for three consecutive days, but September's crush hit a 13-month low, weighing on demand expectations.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin edged up to about $82,178, holding above $82,000 for a second session after Thursday's $1 billion liquidation wave. US spot bitcoin ETFs saw about $145 million of net outflows on Friday. Ethereum slipped to $2,405 as crypto equities took the brunt — Coinbase fell 5.8% and Strategy dropped 9.6% alongside the Nasdaq's 2% decline.
